5.text: The wives of the master refused to live with him; they did not enter the sleeping-room, but staid

19.text: I know of no cases in actual life among the Maritime Chukchee, similar to

20.text: those described above, and occurring among the Reindeer people. It seems that,

21.text: on the whole, the Maritime Chukchee, though more daring in character, are

22.text: of a more peaceful disposition than the Reindeer-breeders. “Nothing ever

23.text: happens among us,” the people in the Chukchee and Eskimo maritime villages

24.text: told me, “though we have no officers. At times of drinking, some of those

25.text: who do not drink act like your police, and quiet down those who become

26.text: aggressive, even binding them if necessary.” Among the Maritime people I

27.text: have even met men who refused to drink brandy; while among the Reindeer-

28.text: breeders such a thing is almost unknown, even among the women, with the

29.text: exception of those in the most remote parts of the country, on the border-line

30.text: of Kamchatka, where no brandy has ever been sold. On the whole, the

31.text: Reindeer Chukchee drink less than the Maritime Chukchee, because brandy

32.text: is more scarce with them; but drunken brawls happen among them much

34.text: In the folk-stories of Maritime provenience, however, “violent men” appear

35.text: quite often; and, in contrast to the Reindeer stories, the violent man is, for

36.text: the most part, the richest man of the village, the front-house master. He is

37.text: successful in his hunt, and has plenty of provisions; but he refuses to give food

38.text: to his poor neighbors, and this is the chief violence he does to them. More-
